checks: Byte-identical to upstream: chat_template.jinja in google/gemma-4-E4B-it at revision ee0ef6023621 equals the text (go run ./tools/feedbuild upstream re-checks it). Last checked 2026-10-14.

Socair's chat-template check (defilantech/socair@ddfe650b5f50, the RealTemplates corpus gate, 2026-10-14): PASS, with no code reach and no content-conditional injection; rendered 6 of 6 probe conversations; text it adds of its own: the <|turn> markers, a system turn when thinking is enabled or tools are given, and tool declaration, call, and response scaffolding; nothing is added under a content condition.
notes: Gemma 4 layout: <|turn>role ... turns after the BOS token, a system turn opened when thinking is enabled, tools are given, or the first message is system or developer, tool declarations written as <|tool>declaration: entries, and tool calls and responses as <|tool_call> and <|tool_response> blocks. Message content may be a list of parts (text, image, audio). Conditions test roles, part types, enable_thinking, and tools; none tests message text. Ends with a newline. The 12B and 31B repositories carry a different text (gemma-4-it).

review.means: A person read the whole template text at the pinned revision and confirmed that it only lays out the conversation it is given: it adds no instruction to the model beyond the publisher's own default system prompt and tool scaffolding, no branch adds text when a message contains a particular string, and it reaches nothing but the documented chat-template variables and filters. Byte identity with the upstream file and Socair's chat-template check are mechanical checks, listed under checks; they are not the review.
